markdown_report:
Choose position-preserving, popularity-matched substitutions with a multiset-preserving swap control before changing BERT4Rec training. At 10% research progress, this remains feasible without unavailable activation hooks.

Starting-point insights: (1) Electronics’ reported training wrong-rank rate reaches 21.97%, motivating investigation without establishing validation weakness. (2) Embedding similarity near 0.5 gives little justification for collapse-focused changes. (3) Compact deletion changes content and positions together. Substitution preserves positions but can introduce implausible content, especially near the prediction mask.

Related-work insights: (1) Zhang and Nanda [1] show that corruption choices and metrics affect intervention conclusions. (2) Heimersheim and Nanda [2] distinguish disruption from restoration; neither identifies a complete mechanism. (3) Krichene and Rendle [3] establish sampled-metric limitations. ROAR [5] additionally motivates caution about distribution shifts introduced by corruption.

These insights suggest three directions: controlled behavioral interventions, internal mechanism localization, and supervision alignment. The framework separates their questions and implementation costs. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Framework position | Scores and critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Matched substitutions plus swap control [1,2,5] | Input disruption: content and arrangement sensitivity | **4/7/5**. Originality: useful control combination; established techniques. Potential: guides revisions; artificial edits may not transfer. Difficulty: existing scoring hooks suffice; support accounting and uncertainty increase integration work. |
| Bidirectional activation patching [1,2] | Component localization: which representations transmit effects? | **5/7/8**. Originality: BERT4Rec adaptation; familiar methodology. Potential: localizes revision candidates; conclusions depend on corruption. Difficulty: hooks may help; architecture details are absent. |
| Endpoint-exposure ablation [4] | Learning alignment: does prefix sampling improve prediction? | **2/6/4**. Originality: explicit exposure control; terminal masking already exists. Potential: directly tests validation gains; baseline equivalence is possible. Difficulty: localized sampler change; retraining consumes budget. |

Selected algorithm: freeze one checkpoint/category. Construct training-only prefixes, append MASK, and compare equal-sized recent/oldest substitutions at unchanged positions. Match donors using predefined training-frequency bins; exclude the original history and entire fixed candidate set. Record donor assignments, unsupported matches and reuse. Also swap recent/oldest blocks while preserving their internal order, exact item multiset, padding and final MASK.

Pseudocode: `freeze checkpoint → fix users/candidates/bins → score baseline → draw paired substitutions and score swap → calculate intervention−baseline and recent−older contrasts → average within user → bootstrap paired users`.

Predefine contrasts and report simultaneous intervals, support counts and matching balance. Separate user variability conditional on realized edits from donor Monte Carlo variability. Swaps test arrangement sensitivity; neither intervention isolates recency from absolute position. Frequency matching does not ensure contextual plausibility or exchangeability. Results concern matchable training-exposed histories; repeated diagnostic selection risks overfitting. Preserve interfaces, predictor consistency, four routes, seeds and host evaluation. No validation improvement is claimed.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255), [3](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/), [4](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690), [5](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2019/file/fe4b8556000d0f0cae99daa5c5c5a410-Paper.pdf).

idea.description: Strengthen the position-preserving, training-popularity-matched recent-versus-older substitution probe with candidate-excluding donors, reproducible matching, explicit support accounting and a multiset-preserving block-swap control. Analyze exactly one independently trained BERT4Rec checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Compact deletion mixes removed content with positional changes. In-place substitution tests identity/content sensitivity at fixed positions, while swapping equal-sized recent and older blocks tests arrangement sensitivity with the exact item multiset preserved. Matching and controls narrow interpretation but do not establish clean-history recency importance, immediate usefulness or causal user preferences. Supplied sensitivity results are incomplete, so no directional effect is assumed.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView interfaces, including item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Use view.model as the actual trained module in evaluation mode without gradients. Capture module modes and global RNG states before diagnostics and restore them in finally. Dedicated diagnostic generators must not consume training RNG. Loader iterator progress and worker-local RNG states cannot generally be restored; disclose that limitation and use a separate diagnostic iterator when available. Preserve loader tuples (None, sequence, positive, negative), B×L shapes, existing masked-target margin probes and embedding diagnostics.

Select up to 200 eligible training users/category with a local seed-42 generator. Eligible users have at least two retained context events before their last training event; report attempted and excluded counts. Set target=history[-1] and prefix=history[:-1][-(L-1):], requiring L>=3. Retain legitimate earlier occurrences of the target item. These are training-exposed recovery fixtures, not untouched validation examples. Append the reserved MASK, left-pad, and read its greatest nonpadding absolute position, never nonpadding count minus one. Require finite scores and an identity-copy check at rtol=1.3e-6, atol=1e-5; record maximum error and halt interpretation of failed fixtures rather than widening tolerances silently.

Before drawing donors, fix each user's auxiliary candidates: include the target once and up to 99 unique real-item negatives sampled using seed 42, excluding the target and all items in the user's supplied training history. If fewer than 99 eligible negatives exist, use all and report the actual count. Reuse this exact candidate array and its order for every intervention; never remove overlapping candidates after editing. Candidates are diagnostic and do not replace pinned host candidates. Rank is one-based with candidate-array order breaking ties. Report target score, target-minus-hardest-negative margin, rank and descriptive HR@10. Define top-10 overlap as intersection size divided by the smaller returned list length; return null with a reason when undefined.

Compute frequency f(i) as the number of occurrences of real catalog item i in supplied training histories, counting repeats and excluding PAD/MASK. Include zero-count catalog items if present in the supplied mapping. Fix bins before examining effects: bin 0 contains f=0; for f>=1, bin b=1+floor(log2(f)) contains counts [2^(b-1),2^b). Save counts, bin edges, boundary conventions, catalog order and bin sizes. These bins are a reproducible design choice, not a published universal threshold. A separately labeled sensitivity analysis may use width-one log bins versus these width-log(2) bins, but cannot select the specification after observing favorable effects.

Choose k=min(3,n//2), giving disjoint oldest and newest blocks. For each replaced occurrence, construct a donor pool containing real items in its original frequency bin, excluding every item in the user's full supplied training history and every fixed candidate. Excluding the full history also excludes the original prefix, removed token and target. Use the same eligibility rule for both blocks. Sort donor IDs before uniform sampling. Draw with replacement across occurrences and replicates; document that donor repetitions can be introduced. Generate ten paired substitution replicates/user with a dedicated seed-42 stream and persist its draw order or per-user/replicate seeds. If either block contains an empty donor pool, the substitution comparison is unavailable for that user under this specification; do not silently widen bins. Record per-token pool sizes, attempted/matched/excluded users and replicates, rejection fractions, failed-match reasons, unique donors and reuse counts. Save every realized original-token/donor assignment. Report donor concentration and effective donor diversity 1/sum(p_d^2), explicitly distinguishing it from the number of independent users.

For each successful paired replicate, replace only the chosen identities in place; retain sequence length, absolute slots, padding, attention visibility and final MASK. Compute recent-minus-baseline and older-minus-baseline effects, then their recent-minus-older contrast. Average replicates within each user before category aggregation. Score a separate swap control that exchanges the oldest and newest k-token blocks while preserving within-block order and middle tokens. This preserves the exact item multiset, popularity counts and repeat multiplicities. Report unchanged swaps as no-ops. Compare substitution and swap results on the common matchable-user subset; report all-eligible-user swap results separately as descriptive support information.

Frequency matching controls a coarse observed property, not contextual plausibility. Preserve the simple frequency-only intervention as the primary specification. As optional subsequent, separately declared analyses, constrain repeat multiplicity or public-history co-occurrence plausibility, or use title/description similarity built only from supplied text without external pretrained weights. These change donor support and the estimand and must not be silently added after inspecting results. Earlier target repeats remain a valid diagnostic stratum. Contextual plausibility and matching support can differ systematically between recent and older positions; larger recent damage can therefore reflect greater corruption severity. Swaps also change item-position associations and local context. Neither intervention alone separates recency, content and learned absolute-position effects. A position-offset probe requires an explicit supported position-ID interface and must otherwise be marked unavailable.

Audit matching with occurrence-weighted raw and log1p frequencies of removed items and realized donors, per block and category; report differences, empirical-CDF discrepancies and standardized mean differences when variances permit. Report null for undefined balance summaries. Assess retained-versus-excluded users by history length, target training frequency and repeat status, with recorded cutpoints and counts. Do not interpret good balance as exchangeability or infer unobserved selection bias. Aggregate users with equal weight and replicates equally within user; do not import observational causal-matching multiplicity weights that would change this diagnostic estimand. Donor reuse is recorded; conditional-on-realized-donors user intervals do not quantify uncertainty from resampling a shared donor pool.

Predefine the inferential family before execution: four contrasts (recent−baseline, older−baseline, recent−older, swap−baseline), three outcomes (margin, rank, HR@10), and four categories, yielding 48 contrasts where all are defined. Use 20,000 seed-42 paired-user bootstrap resamples with identical user indices across contrasts within each category. Report ordinary percentile 95% intervals as exploratory and Bonferroni percentile intervals at tail probabilities 0.05/(2*48) and 1-0.05/(2*48) for approximate familywise coverage; retain the planned denominator if some contrasts are unavailable. State finite-bootstrap tail resolution and the approximate nature of bootstrap coverage. Stratum summaries, target scores and overlap remain descriptive unless added to the inferential family in advance. No ordinary interval becomes simultaneous through adjusted p-values.

The bootstrap conditions on the fitted checkpoint, selected users, fixed candidates and realized donors. Separately report donor Monte Carlo standard errors for substitution means by computing each paired replicate's category mean and its across-replicate standard deviation divided by sqrt(10); label ten-draw precision as limited. These estimates concern donor sampling conditional on users and candidates, not total uncertainty. Do not mechanically add them to user-bootstrap intervals. Optional additional candidate draws use predefined seeds 43 and 44, rebuild donor pools to exclude each entire candidate set, and report results separately with changed support counts. Candidate changes necessarily also change donor eligibility, so this sensitivity analysis does not isolate candidate randomness alone. Keep the pinned benchmark unchanged.

Return null plus explicit reasons for missing observations, empty pools, unsupported hooks or failed checks. Retain empty category-metadata breakdowns because categories are unavailable. Keep review content, ratings, commercial attributes and simulator traits unavailable. Do not infer ownership, compatibility, mood, replacement need or immediate utility. Include measured metrics, definitions, counts, assignment provenance, exposure labels, uncertainty scope and unavailable reasons in diagnosis_interpreter_prompt. Repeatedly consulting these training diagnostics or validation outcomes can overfit the search; preregister a bounded diagnostic specification and host-supported selection policy, log adaptive queries, and avoid choosing interventions or bins for favorable effects.

No architecture change is required. Preserve checkpoint configuration and the embedded predictor writer; a diagnostic live-score check does not establish fresh-process predictor/checkpoint parity. Mark that check unavailable unless the host supplies a reload runner. Retain all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per completed epoch. All host execution, including diagnostics and failures, consumes the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Only host-supported four-category macro validation HR@10 selects revisions; auxiliary metrics do not substitute for it. Preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the twenty designated training users, five/category, and describe their coverage and frequency distribution as exposure rather than accuracy. Deploy exactly one checkpoint per category, without averaging, independently fitted scorers or score fusion.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        state = capture_module_modes_and_global_rng_states()
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                metrics, definitions = existing_family_safe_diagnostics(train_loader)
                counts = training_occurrence_counts(self.view.user_train)
                bins = fixed_log2_frequency_bins(counts)
                users = select_eligible_training_users(limit=200, seed=42)
                rows, assignments, failures = [], [], []
                for user in users:
                    history = supplied_training_history(user)
                    target = history[-1]
                    prefix = history[:-1][-(L - 1):]
                    if L < 3 or len(prefix) < 2:
                        record_ineligible(user)
                        continue
                    candidates = fixed_auxiliary_candidates(
                        target=target, exclude=set(history),
                        unique_negatives=99, seed=42)
                    clean = left_pad(prefix + [MASK], L)
                    readout = greatest_nonpadding_absolute_index(clean)
                    baseline = score(self.view, clean, readout, candidates)
                    require_finite_and_identity_copy_parity(baseline, clean, candidates)
                    k = min(3, len(prefix) // 2)
                    blocks = {
                        'older': list(range(k)),
                        'recent': list(range(len(prefix) - k, len(prefix)))
                    }
                    excluded = set(history) | set(candidates) | {PAD, MASK}
                    pools = {
                        position: sorted_same_bin_catalog_items(
                            prefix[position], bins, exclude=excluded)
                        for position in blocks['older'] + blocks['recent']
                    }
                    record_pool_sizes_and_support(user, pools)
                    swapped = swap_equal_end_blocks(prefix, k, preserve_internal_order=True)
                    swap_scores = score_unchanged_layout(swapped, clean, readout, candidates)
                    swap_effect = outcomes(swap_scores) - outcomes(baseline)
                    if any(len(pool) == 0 for pool in pools.values()):
                        record_unmatchable_user_and_reason(user)
                        rows.append(swap_only_descriptive_row(user, swap_effect))
                        continue
                    replicate_effects = []
                    for replicate in range(10):
                        results = {}
                        for name, block in blocks.items():
                            edited = list(prefix)
                            for position in block:
                                donor = uniform_choice(pools[position], diagnostic_rng)
                                edited[position] = donor
                                assignments.append(
                                    (user, replicate, name, position,
                                     prefix[position], donor, len(pools[position])))
                            tokens = left_pad(edited + [MASK], L)
                            assert_same_padding_positions_and_final_mask(clean, tokens)
                            scores = score(self.view, tokens, readout, candidates)
                            results[name] = outcomes(scores) - outcomes(baseline)
                        replicate_effects.append({
                            'recent-baseline': results['recent'],
                            'older-baseline': results['older'],
                            'recent-older': results['recent'] - results['older']
                        })
                    rows.append({
                        'user': user,
                        'effects': mean_within_user(replicate_effects),
                        'replicate_effects': replicate_effects,
                        'swap-baseline': swap_effect,
                        'strata': recorded_training_only_strata(user, prefix, target)
                    })
                persist_trial_local_assignments_counts_and_failures(assignments, failures)
                metrics.update(equal_user_aggregation(rows))
                metrics.update(paired_user_bootstrap(
                    rows, resamples=20000, seed=42,
                    shared_indices_across_contrasts=True,
                    exploratory_level=0.95, planned_family_size=48))
                metrics.update(separate_donor_monte_carlo_errors(rows))
                metrics.update(support_balance_reuse_and_descriptive_strata(rows, assignments))
                definitions.update(exposure_matching_candidate_and_uncertainty_definitions())
                return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}
        finally:
            restore_module_modes_and_global_rng_states(state)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return grounded_prompt(
        raw_diagnosis,
        require=['measured evidence', 'definitions', 'counts', 'support',
                 'uncertainty scope', 'unavailable reasons'],
        distinguish=['training-exposed sensitivity', 'host validation',
                     'content disruption', 'arrangement sensitivity',
                     'qualitative hypotheses'],
        prohibit=['invented preferences', 'causal utility claims',
                  'generalizing matched subsets without assumptions',
                  'ensemble proposals'])

originality.positive: Combines candidate-excluding matched substitutions, fixed-position comparisons and multiset-preserving swaps within the BERT4Rec diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Matching, substitution and permutation controls are established methods; the contribution is a careful diagnostic adaptation rather than a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: Can produce more interpretable evidence for focused single-model training experiments by separating content disruption, arrangement sensitivity and matching-support limitations.
future_potential.negative: Training exposure, artificial histories and absolute-position effects limit conclusions; diagnostic agreement does not demonstrate improved validation ranking or immediate usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing sequence encoding and scoring hooks suffice, and no architecture change or retraining is required.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible donor assignments, candidate exclusions, support accounting, paired aggregation, multiplicity control and separate uncertainty sources make the earlier difficulty rating of 3 too optimistic.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Examines how corruption procedures and evaluation metrics affect activation-patching conclusions.
Motivates explicit intervention controls and multiple ranking diagnostics.
limitations: Studies language models rather than this BERT4Rec benchmark.
Does not establish that popularity-matched substitutions improve recommendation accuracy.

related_work.title: How to Use and Interpret Activation Patching
contributions: Distinguishes restoration and disruption experiments and discusses interpretation limits.
Supports labeling substitution effects as disruption evidence.
limitations: Does not supply a verified BERT4Rec intervention implementation.
Intervention sensitivity alone cannot establish user preferences or complete mechanism identification.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics.
Supports keeping auxiliary candidate diagnostics separate from benchmark selection.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator.
Does not quantify sampling distortion for the supplied checkpoints.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the masked-target and appended-mask formulation that the proposed probe preserves.
limitations: Terminal masking is existing methodology and cannot support a novelty claim by itself.
Does not establish that this task's qualitative failures arise from recent-history underuse.

related_work.title: A Benchmark for Interpretability Methods in Deep Neural Networks
contributions: Introduces ROAR and addresses distribution shifts caused by removing input features.
Motivates caution when interpreting performance damage under corrupted histories.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed sequential-recommendation interventions.
Retraining changes the model being explained and is outside this frozen-checkpoint probe.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling that preserves aligned observations.
Supports resampling users jointly across baseline and intervention outcomes.
limitations: Does not select the correct sampling unit or uncertainty estimand automatically.
Repeated donor draws are not independent users, and conditional bootstrap intervals omit candidate and training uncertainty.

related_work.title: MatchIt documentation: Coarsened Exact Matching and Assessing Balance
contributions: Explains matching through explicitly coarsened covariate strata and common support.
Motivates recording bin definitions, unsupported observations and balance diagnostics.
limitations: Observational causal-matching estimands and weights do not automatically apply to frozen-model perturbations.
Frequency-bin matching does not ensure plausible replacement histories or exchangeability.

related_work.title: R documentation: Adjust P-values for Multiple Comparisons
contributions: Documents familywise multiple-testing procedures including Bonferroni and Holm.
Supports distinguishing adjusted hypothesis tests from simultaneous interval construction.
limitations: Adjusted p-values do not make ordinary 95% confidence intervals simultaneous.
Multiplicity correction does not address adaptive specification selection or intervention validity.
